note: Four curve values per parameter (the defaults of the sheet), the parameter that is varied first, a line on what the parameter does, and the first three moments as expressions in the parameters a, b, c, d of explorer-families.json. A moment that does not exist reads "undefined" or "infinite".

parameters.effect: Location: slides the whole curve along x. Its shape, spread and tails do not change.
Scale: the standard deviation. A larger value spreads the curve, lowers its peak and fattens both tails; the area stays 1.
Location of ln X: multiplies the whole curve by exp(value), so it moves right and spreads, with the same shape.
Dispersion of ln X: a larger value skews the curve to the right and thickens the right tail sharply.
Degrees of freedom: few degrees give heavy tails and a sharp centre; many approach the Normal. The mean needs more than 1, the variance more than 2.
Degrees of freedom: the mean equals the value and the variance twice it; the curve moves right, spreads and becomes more symmetric.
Numerator degrees of freedom: more degrees narrow the curve around 1 and lighten the right tail.
Denominator degrees of freedom: few degrees give a heavy right tail; the mean needs more than 2, the variance more than 4.
Shape: below 1 the density is unbounded at 0; at 1 it is the exponential; larger values give a bell-like, less skewed curve.
Scale: stretches the curve along x without changing its shape; the mean and the standard deviation grow in proportion.
Alpha: larger values move the mass towards 1; below 1 the density is unbounded at 0.
Beta: larger values move the mass towards 0; below 1 the density is unbounded at 1.
Rate: the mean is 1/rate. A larger rate concentrates the mass near 0 and shortens the right tail.
Shape: below 1 the hazard falls and the tail is heavy; at 1 it is the exponential; above 1 the curve is bell-like and the tail lightens.
Scale: stretches the curve along x; about 63% of the mass lies below the value.
Lower bound: moves the left end; the height is 1/(upper - lower), so the curve gets taller as the interval narrows.
Upper bound: moves the right end; a longer interval lowers the curve and raises the variance.
Trials: the mean grows with the number of trials and the distribution becomes more symmetric.
Probability of success: moves the mean and sets the skew; below 0.5 the right tail is longer, above 0.5 the left.
Mean: also the variance. A larger mean moves the mass right, spreads it and makes it more symmetric.
Probability of success: a smaller value lengthens the right tail; the count is the failures before the first success.
Target successes: more successes move the mean right and make the distribution more symmetric.
Probability of success: a smaller value lengthens the right tail and raises the variance.
Sample size: a larger sample moves the mean right and, relative to the binomial, reduces the variance by the finite-population factor.
Population successes: moves the mean right; the distribution is symmetric when successes are half the population.
Population size: a larger population with the same successes lowers the success share, so the mean falls and the curve approaches the binomial.
Lower bound: moves the left end; a longer range lowers every probability, 1/(upper - lower + 1).
Upper bound: moves the right end; a longer range lowers every probability and raises the variance.
